observations.text: The interview consistently identifies Randy's mother as Mama, his primary caregiver and comfort source, but does not provide her first name, age, occupation, or education.
Shared activities such as bedtime reading, school folder routine, doctor visits, church, drawing dinosaurs, and comfort during worry are supported by the interview.
The mother entry aligns with the profile's description of Randy's mother as first comfort source, school routine manager, health information explainer, and daily household caregiver.
The interview identifies Randy's father as Daddy and strongly supports the father relationship, but does not provide his first name, age, occupation, or education.
The cited evidence supports Daniel's role in toy disassembly, LEGO building, tool names, and solving toy problems.
The father entry aligns with the profile's father-as-tool-and-building-mentor pattern and Randy's hands-on mechanical interests.

The interview supports Grandma as a visitor, support figure, coin giver, and person Randy sometimes tells exciting news to, but does not provide her first name, side of family, exact age, occupation, education, or Jonesboro location.
The evidence citations support the grandmother relationship and coin-giving, but the exact label 'Dodd side' is not established.
The grandmother entry matches the profile's support-figure and nearby-family description, including Grandma as someone Randy tells exciting news to and someone who gives coins.
Mason is explicitly named as a school friend who likes trucks, but his last name, age, gender, location, and education details are inferred.
Shared activities involving trucks, block towers, racing, dirt roads, and minor child arguments are supported by the interview's school friend and recess descriptions.
The Mason entry aligns with the profile's documented school friendship, truck interest, recess play, classmates, and age-graded peer world.
The interview strongly supports nearby cousins as frequent playmates, but no cousin is named; Eli Johnson's name, age, gender, and demographics are invented beyond the record.
The cousin shared activities are supported: chase, hide-and-seek, porch-to-tree races, crawfish boils, birthdays, and after-church visits.
The cousin entry aligns with the profile's repeated emphasis on cousins as weekend, after-church, and family-gathering playmates.

circle_level_observations.text: The interview repeatedly identifies Randy's teacher as an important daily support figure who helps with learning, puzzles, kindergarten adjustment, and comfort when he misses Mama. The five-member draft omits the teacher, but the circle already contains five strongly supported ties, including both parents, Grandma, named friend Mason, and cousins.
The soccer coach is mentioned as important but less central than parents, Grandma, Mason, cousins, and teacher; omission from a five-person circle is acceptable.

verification.verdict_rationale: All entries agree with the interview and corrected profile. Several names, demographics, and communication details are inferred rather than directly stated, but they do not contradict the source material and are carried forward as plausible inference gaps. No revisions or human review are required.
verification.final_status: The social circle is verified and ready for downstream use.

demographics.education: high school graduate with some postsecondary coursework

Photos or notes about Randy reading new words at night and drawing dinosaurs.
Reassurance about thunder, shots, and kindergarten worries, often with simple comfort messages.
